summary: The note argues that soft skills such as empathy, teamwork, communication and emotional intelligence have become a critical asset in the local job market as of late 2023. It cites surveys, reports, training initiatives and local professionals showing links between soft skills and growth, productivity, diversity outcomes, leadership and resilience to automation. It concludes that soft skills will keep gaining importance in shaping employment trends.
one_line: Soft skills like empathy, communication and adaptability are becoming the key differentiator in local hiring, education, leadership and automation-era work as of late 2023.
key_facts: Oliver Thompson, Lead HR Analyst at Local Dynamics, said on November 5, 2023 that employers now advocate as fiercely, if not more so, for soft skills than hard skills.
Thompson said, "These are the skills that machines cannot replicate," calling the human element the competitive edge.
A Nielsen survey released on September 15, 2023 found 73% of CEOs in the local region believe a lack of employees with soft skills could devastate future growth prospects.
The Local Skills Training Initiative (LSTI), introduced in late September 2023, engages students in problem-solving tasks, group projects and community outreach programs to build soft skills.
Dr. Jane McKenna, program director of LSTI, groups soft skills into social skills, personal traits and problem-solving abilities.
A McKinley & Associates report of October 20, 2023 found proficiency in soft skills leads to better job performance, more capacity for leadership roles and more team collaboration.
Jessica Sanders, Regional Manager of GreenTech Solutions, reported on December 1, 2023 that a soft skills program improved internal communication and project management exponentially.
Brian O'Reilly, a local sales manager, attributes his career progression to improving active listening and empathy about two years ago, which brought in new clients.
A Human Capital Benchmarking report released on November 23, 2023 found organizations with diversified teams and strong soft skills emphasis were 35% more likely to outperform competitors.

A Leadership Skills Academy survey conducted on September 30, 2023 found executives and managers are frequently assessed for soft skills such as emotional intelligence, constructive feedback and conflict resolution.
Tucker Lee, AI Consultant for TechForward, said soft skills buffer against the potential adverse effects of automation.
Maria Gutierrez, Head of Diversity and Inclusion at Securitas Financial, said navigating and embracing diversity through soft skills is paramount in a multicultural society.
Mentorship programs, soft skills workshops and community forums and networks are becoming standard ways to develop soft skills.
